solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In the City, unfortunately, half feel the need to get away?

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
half of the word feel is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A city worker, feeling hemmed in, half wishes to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'unfortunately' uses THE CITY plus FE (half of 'feel') to make the two words; 'In' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for a restless urge to travel or move on.

clue.text: Jot letter from Athens

definitions.meaning: a jot is a tiny amount, a whit
a Greek letter, the ninth of that alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles a note taken from a letter sent from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter has become an idiom for the smallest possible amount, just like a jot.

clue.text: Song about one beginning to imbibe wine

indicators.note: about means the song's letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: a chant is a song, especially a repetitive one
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the word imbibe

explanation.surface: A drinking song strikes up as someone starts to down their wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany, named after the hills where it is made.

clue.text: Bovine chatter

definitions.meaning: a long-haired ox of Tibet, a member of the cattle family
informal word for talking at length, as a verb

explanation.surface: Cows that gossip — a silly picture of chattering cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan ox is a bovine; as a verb the same word is slang for talking incessantly.

clue.text: Amount canvas destroyed?

parts.note: something destroyed is former, no more: an ex-
a tent is made of canvas

explanation.surface: Asking how much canvas was ruined in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: A destroyed tent is cryptically an 'ex-tent', a tent that used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the size, scope or degree of something, i.e. its amount.

clue.text: Being behind, rise, stand another way

indicators.note: arranged another way means the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a late-comer: get up and stand differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness: being behind schedule is a state of delay.

clue.text: Go down quietly — I had returned

indicators.note: returned means the contraction is turned back to front

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, giving ID
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone sank out of view without a sound after coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in answer order: the reversed DI first, then P, despite 'quietly' coming first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip is to sink or drop lower, a synonym of descend.

clue.text: Author due to lose heart over enemy

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word due is dropped

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A writer who is about to give up hope over a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places DE above FOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Quite attractive

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning fairly or rather, as in 'fairly good'

explanation.surface: Reads as a mild compliment: rather good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means fairly; as an adjective it means pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Pass round back of biggish group of trees

indicators.note: round means the pass goes around the next piece

parts.note: a ticket is a pass granting entry

indicators.note: back of picks out the final letter of the word biggish

explanation.surface: Someone walks past and round a fairly big clump of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense clump of bushes or small trees, a kind of copse.

clue.text: Gun found in holster: I fled

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the words holster: I fled

explanation.surface: A fugitive's weapon is discovered in a holster after they fled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, an example of a gun.

clue.text: Refusing to move, nine starting to budge

indicators.note: to budge is to shift, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Nine stubborn people starting to give way, which contradicts the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refusing to move' and 'to budge' pull in opposite directions, hiding the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent describes someone stubborn, unwilling to change their position.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasant being mutinous?

definitions.meaning: rising up in rebellion; the question mark flags the less common sense

explanation.surface: A sailor's view of a nasty, rebellious crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means disgusting, and also, literally, rising in revolt as mutineers do.

clue.text: Capital where king is evidently venerated, initially

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of each of the four words king is evidently venerated

explanation.surface: A capital city where a monarch is plainly revered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian spelling of the capital of Ukraine, now usually written Kyiv.

clue.text: Test: most ending in failure rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the most

indicators.note: ending in picks out the last letter of the word failure

explanation.surface: A test that most people fail, leading to rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal assessment, a synonym of a test.

clue.text: While a coil fixed, detached

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I walked'

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of doctored or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coil was repaired while a part came loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding others, i.e. aloof and withdrawn from company.

clue.text: Companion from different sector

indicators.note: different means the letters are made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A companion arrives from another part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is someone who accompanies another, a companion or chaperone.

clue.text: Country where simple abode found in block

indicators.note: found in means the dwelling sits inside the word for block

parts.note: to ban is to block or prohibit
a hut is a simple dwelling

explanation.surface: A land where a basic home stands in a city block.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a small Himalayan kingdom, a nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Extraordinary athletes present — beat them all?

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to show is to present or display

explanation.surface: Remarkable sportspeople on display outshine everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to outshine all the other performers, attracting the most attention.

clue.text: Girl upon wings of drake, duck

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: wings of picks out the two outside letters of the word drake

explanation.surface: A girl perched on a male duck's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a verb here, not the bird the drake suggests; 'upon' just stacks the girl above the wings in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge or avoid something, a synonym of evade.

clue.text: See some sketches, Pythonesque

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Watch a few Monty Python-style comedy sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for spot.

clue.text: Asian lady's heading off before one

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a lady is a woman; the 's stands for 'has'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman sets off ahead of someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Omani describes a person from Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula in Asia.

clue.text: Worst thing, this pet running wild

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An owner despairs of a pet that has got loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that is the very worst, the lowest of the low.

clue.text: Failing to start, expensive sound processing unit

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: A pricey piece of audio equipment that won't switch on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like hi-fi kit but describes a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing takes in sound and processes it, wittily called a unit.

clue.text: Listen to Asian link

indicators.note: listen to says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a Thai is someone from Thailand in Asia

explanation.surface: Hear about a connection with someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a bond or connection between things.

clue.text: Source of personal information has to improve, as a rule

parts.note: a gene carries the hereditary information that makes a person who they are
to rally is to recover or improve

explanation.surface: A database of personal details must get better, as is customary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of personal information' suggests a database or file, but it is a unit of DNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally means usually or in most cases, the same as 'as a rule'.
